analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor (Nov 20, 2026)
key_insights: SPX fell 8.6% on the week to 6,910 (below 7,000) and NDX fell 10.4%, its worst week since March 2020, as investors grew wary of the AI trade. SPX has closed lower 7 straight sessions, the longest streak since Feb 2020 and one of 5 instances in 25 years.
Defensives, bond proxies and homebuilders outperformed on the week. Drones, quantum computing and neoclouds posted the largest basket losses (about -23% to -25%).

Hedge funds net sold US equities for a third straight week (6 of the last 7), driven by heavy single-stock shorting. US single stocks were shorted every day this week, the largest weekly shorting since June 2022. ETF short flows rose 11.1%, the largest percentage shorting since March.

9 of 11 US sectors were net sold (Info Tech and Energy excepted). Financials was the most net sold sector in dollar and SD terms (-2.2 SDs, short sales about 7x long buys), at the fastest pace in more than five years. Energy was the most net bought (+1.4 SDs), the largest percentage net buying in over 7 months.

US Fundamental L/S net leverage is 44.8% (5th percentile one-year). Beta-adjusted gross leverage of 208.8% is a 3-year low and beta-adjusted net leverage of 54.6% is in the 1st percentile over 3 years.

Shares desk: high-touch activity was not in proportion to the size of the moves. The desk points to ETFs at over 39% of Friday's tape and thin top-of-book liquidity (S&P at $4mm, near YTD low). Long-only sell tickets in semis are steady with buyers 'frozen', and 'panic' is described as anecdotal but intensifying. The main debate is what catalyst could put a bottom in.

Late-Friday headlines added pressure: an SEC probe related to NVDA, hawkish Washington officials, and a report (FT) of Israel urging Trump to restart strikes on Iran. This followed capital markets activity that did not stabilize risk appetite.

Futures desk: CTAs are estimated net short US equities by $19bn after selling $57bn over the past month. CTA forecasts show selling in every scenario next week, with SPX trigger levels of 7596 / 7540 / 7119 (short/medium/long term).

Equity funding: the December S&P TRF held near FF+35 for two weeks and fell to about FF+20 on Friday. Year-end funding (Z6-F7 spread) held near FF+100 but may fade if the drawdown continues. HFs covered about 68k contracts (~$25bn) of index shorts from 11/10 to 11/19.

High grade copper futures fell more than 9% on tighter financial conditions and data center weakness, triggering CTA selling. Producer/merchant gross longs were near multiyear highs on Nov 10, which limited physical buying capacity.

Derivatives desk: equity vol is in extreme stress. VIX is above 35, term structure is aggressively inverted, skew is steep, and the GS US vol panic index is 9.8/10. Readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief. The one-week VIX move was the fifth largest on record.

NDX is more than 20% below its high and oversold (14-day RSI 26.5). Gamma is short with no support to the downside, so large moves are expected to continue. The desk sees CTA NDX positioning near the bottom of its 10-year range and calls this 'closer to the end than the beginning', though CFTC non-dealer positioning remains near highs.

Derivatives desk bottom line: technicals point to a near-term bounce, but further out the market faces challenges until there is clarity on the Fed's path and the future of the AI trade. The desk cites aggressive financial conditions tightening, the AI unwind, overseas tensions, and a tightening cycle signaled by the Fed.

Baskets desk draws a 4Q 2018 analog. High-Beta Cyclicals (GSXUHBCY) are up 12% YTD while US AI (GSTMTAIP) is negative on the year. In 4Q18 high-beta cyclicals fell 23% and underperformed SPX by 10pp. Their 15x forward P/E is a 40% premium to the basket's 2018 trough multiple.

The Lending Sensitive basket (GSXULEND) is flat QTD versus -15% in 4Q18 and is exposed to Fed hawkishness. The desk's preferred long is the High vs Low FCF pair (GSPUFCFP), also GSPEFCFP in Europe. European consumer baskets (GSXEUKCO, GSXEDCON, both +12% QTD) fell 28% and 16% in 4Q18.

TMT: SOX fell 17% on the week, its worst since Sept 2011, and is down 33% since the start of October. NDX trades at 17x forward P/E and semis at about 12-13x, valuations at 10-year lows. Fundamentals are described as healthy (KEYS, NVDA and PANW beat and raised), but there is no identifiable catalyst and buyers are on strike.

Healthcare: managed care led weakness on the CRUSH/RADV proposal, calls for a vertical break-up and renewed Medicare-for-All headlines, spreading to services, hospitals, medtech and biopharma. INSM/SNY M&A headlines had only marginal impact.

Industrials and materials fell almost 700bps on the week. SMID levered industrials were hit hard: TROX -42%, YSS -35%, FLY -30%, FMC -22%, and MTZ -20% after a surprise leverage-raising deal. VRT, FPS and INIO fell 18%. ACM rose 12% on earnings and 2027 guidance, and housing names outperformed on lower rates.

Energy: Brent is down 15% over the past month, with 2027 oversupply risk and weaker DOE product stats easing diesel concerns. Refining is the most shorted subsector in desk conversations. Natural gas is a well-owned hiding spot, and E&Ps are preferred over midstream.

Next week: S&P implied move through 11/27 is 3.27%. Earnings include DELL, WDAY, HPQ (Tuesday night), BBY, DKS, BURL, DLTR, ANF, URBN, plus ADI, ADSK, NTNX, ZM, HPE, SMTC, and DE. PCE is the key macro print. US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close at 1pm Friday.

tension_points.theme: AI selloff bounce vs further downside
tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is washed out, the vol panic index is 9.8/10 (above 9.5 has signaled near-term relief), NDX RSI is 26.5, valuations are at 10-year lows, fundamentals are firm (NVDA, KEYS, PANW beat and raise), and CTA NDX positioning is near its 10-year low, which the desk sees as closer to the end than the beginning.
tension_points.bear_case: There is no identifiable catalyst, buyers are on strike, gamma is short with no downside support, CTAs are forecast to sell in every scenario, FCI is the tightest in over 2 years, and the Fed is signaling tightening. CFTC non-dealer positioning remains near highs, and the 2018 analog points to further downside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further CTA selling through the SPX trigger levels of 7596 / 7540 / 7119 and a continued drawdown that erodes the Z6-F7 funding premium would extend the downside.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth optimism remains high and the market has rotated out of AI into ex-AI rather than owning outright equity downside, leaving high-beta cyclicals up 12% YTD.
tension_points.bear_case: If growth uncertainty takes over from inflation anxiety, as in 4Q 2018 when the basket fell 23%, a 15x forward P/E (40% above the 2018 trough multiple) leaves this pocket exposed to sharp underperformance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth uncertainty overtaking inflation anxiety, as happened in 4Q 2018.
